items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: She was the English wife of Ali Kahn who became Princess Ali Khan and the mother of Prince Karim the present Aga Khan.

ctx.x: sailed out into the bay and after dinner Ali Kahn wanted to take his clothes off and dive in the bay from the highest deck and swim around the boat. It was said that that was high delight whenever he went out on a boating party. But he was restrained that night because it was rumoured that there were sharks in the bay and they could have been attracted by the lights of the boat although we did not see any.

Another wonderful thing about that night is that during one of the intermissions I was sitting on an upholstered bench near the bandstand and a beautiful blonde-haired lady was sitting on the same bench and she started talking to me. What the conversation was I don't remember but I remember this lady was very nice. Later I excused myself and got on the bandstand. Someone asked me if I knew who the lady was that I had been talking to and when they told me I could have been knocked over with a feather. She was the…

The six months in Bombay passed very fast and on April the 27th 1937, we left India on the Conte-Rosso which was an Italian boat headed for Venice and another world. Teddy Weatherford had never been in Europe and had decided that he was coming back with us. Charlie Lewis brought his girl Ivy back with him and we landed in Venice the 8th of May and the next day we were in Paris. The trip was great coming back the same as it had been going, but Beezie and I had a cabin to ourselves on the boat.
